results.name: Legacy CSV guards also cover the same leading-dot bug with leading zeros and other C# fields
Leading-dot ternary extracts 0.75 and a binding that includes its decimal point; null access and strings remain opaque
Unity source patches round-trip decimals, zero, one and explicit 75 without a stray decimal point or changing the other branch
Local restart corrects only an unedited legacy CSV baseline from 75 to 0.75 and stamps new exports
New regular CSV stages and applies 0.8; old unmarked 75 CSV is rejected without changing source or saved drafts
New transfer CSV carries before 0.75/value 0.8 and imports/applies correctly; old parser CSV cannot reintroduce 75
An explicitly new-format 75 is serialized as 75f, rather than 0.75 or malformed .75 text
Cloud migration persists 0.75 once, rotates stale revision and preserves all unrelated saved edits and source hashes
A custom legacy edit is preserved and shown as a conflict instead of silently rescaling or deleting it
Active bridge work is neither cancelled nor rewritten; legacy correction waits, then completes after the lease work finishes
Hosted normal and transfer CSV exports contain the corrected decimals and reject legacy 75 imports
Bridge applies and proves the correct decimal in a copied project; stale/malformed old parser claims cannot prove an apply
Authenticated web requests complete 0.75 -> 0.8 -> 0.75 through actual bridge leases, source writes and verified public acknowledgements
